questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to improve my english, and I wanted to go far away. Furthermore I didn't know too much about Australia, so I thought it'd be a great opportunity to learn and see a lot of new things. I choose Sydney, because I wanted to live in a big city.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy. There's lots of numbers to call, but I didn't remember needing them.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: University of Sydney provided a free pickup from the airport to my accomodation, and that was great.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I went to University of Sydney's website where they had links to accomodation on and off campus. It was very easy to find accomodation, but I was also out super early (in April I think, and I left for exchange in late July). Student accomodations are super expensive, and I didnt find it as social as I would have expected, but I also realised that I didnt need it, since there's lots of other options to socialize. Therefore,  I'll probably recommend finding a room in a house in one of the many Facebook groups there are. They're also usually more social, or at least that's what my impression is.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You won't miss out by living off campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very expensive.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Easy enough. However, sometimes quite a long waiting time to get a reply over mail from my Study Abroad Adviser, but the answers were always very detailed and helpful.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was numbers to call, sometimes I called someone wrong, but then I was referred. Also mailing my Study Abroad Adviser from USYD.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got registered in the classes that I wanted to take - except for one class because of a prerequisite that I didn't fulfill, but then I just applied for another unit, which was easy enough.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Read the mails carefully and get your stuff done before the deadlines.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A bit too easy units (but maybe I just choose them too easy). Very good communication from USYD's side, and you can get a lot of help.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I was doing my 5th semester abroad, where I did three 2nd year units and one 1st year unit.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Less self studying abroad, they are very thorough with explaining concepts and you get a lot of practice by doing the tutorials.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: AREC2005, MATH2023, FINC2011, QBUS1040

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: AREC2005 was interesting (and easy to pass). You learn some Python in QBUS1040, and they hold your hand all the way.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Experiences are more expensive than what I first imagined, and alcohol is super expensive (200DKK for the cheapest bottle of vodka 70cl)

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Alcohol and parties were more expensive, transportation was less expensive. I didnt have to buy books, which was also a pleasant surprise.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: LOTS of clubs.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: So so many, like more than 200 clubs.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Anything tbh, just try some new stuff out that'll challenge you (but dont beat yourself up if you end up going less than expected)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Blue mountains, beaches. Just nature stuff in general. Do trips with friends or solo and enjoy.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy enough, like 8/10 easiness.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just go and talk to them, sit next to someone you think looks local in class.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Australians wake up super early and party early and cafe's arent open in the afternoon.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The beach life, the chill vibe. The shortenings are also funny.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Try to join a club.
Don't be afraid to sit next to someone in class.
Don't be afraid to ask for help.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Hmm, ABS cafeteria has lunch for 6 bucks if you have the USYD app (hopefully also when you get there, but at least when I was there). Lectures are almost always recorded and most units doesn't take attendance, but check for every single unit.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting the people I met and the trips I went on (e.g. in midsem break)

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Accepting that there's things in Denmark I'll miss out on. And finding the sweet spot to how much I should study vs free time.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
